A clerk, The Copyist

A STORY OF A STREET.

by the author




I am a rather elderly man. The nature of my avocations for the last
many years has brought me into more than ordinary contact with what
would seem an interesting and somewhat singular set of men, of whom as
yet nothing that I know of has ever been written:—I mean the
copyists or clerks. I have known very many of them,
professionally and privately, and if I pleased, could relate divers
histories, at which good-natured gentlemen might smile, and sentimental
souls might weep. But I waive the biographies of all other clerks
for a few passages in the life of a clerk, who was a clerk of the
strangest I ever saw or heard of. While of other copyists I might
write the complete life, of a clerk nothing of that sort can be done.
